query: VS Code for the Web limitations no terminal web extensions supported capabilities
answer: VS Code for the Web does not support terminal web extensions or capabilities due to its browser-based nature, which inherently limits certain functionalities such as running a terminal or debugger. The browser environment restricts running code that requires a runtime environment, like compiling or debugging Rust or Go applications. Only a subset of extensions can run in the web version, and those that require a terminal or other unsupported features will not be available. The sources indicate that for full capabilities, including terminal access and running unsupported extensions, users are recommended to switch to the desktop application or GitHub Codespaces.

## Limitations

Since VS Code for the Web runs completely within the browser, some experiences will naturally be more constrained when compared to what you can do in the desktop app. For example, the terminal and debugger are not available, which makes sense since you can't compile, run, and debug a Rust or Go application within the browser sandbox.

### Extensions

Only a subset of extensions can run in the browser. You can use the Extensions view to install extensions in the web, and extensions that cannot be installed will have a warning icon and Learn Why link. We expect more extensions to become enabled over time. [...] ## Relationship to VS Code Desktop

VS Code for the Web provides a browser-based experience for navigating files and repositories and committing lightweight code changes. However, if you need access to a runtime to run, build, or debug your code, you want to use platform features such as a terminal, or you want to run extensions that aren't supported in the web, we recommend moving your work to the desktop application, GitHub Codespaces, or using Remote - Tunnels for the full capabilities of VS Code. In addition, VS Code Desktop lets you use a full set of keyboard shortcuts not limited by your browser.

When you're ready to switch, you'll be able to "upgrade" to the full VS Code experience with a few clicks. [...] VS Code for the Web has many of the features of VS Code Desktop that you love, including search and syntax highlighting while browsing and editing, along with extension support to work on your codebase and make simpler edits. In addition to opening repositories, forks, and pull requests from source control providers like GitHub and Azure Repos, you can also work with code that is stored on your local machine.

VS Code for the Web runs entirely in your web browser, so there are certain limitations compared to the desktop experience, which you can read more about below.

Next, in the Settings dropdown, select Reset User Settings.
